errors.text: The proposed material family is a generic refractory HEA rather than the as-cast AlCoCrFeNi2.1 eutectic HEA with FCC and B2 phases.

The hypothesis changes the controlling variable from aging temperature to aging time and therefore does not reconstruct the approximately 550–750 °C brittle window or the 600 °C minimum and 750 °C recovery.
It attributes recovery to precipitate coarsening and loss of coherency instead of reduced L12 ordering and formation of ductile transition zones along B2/FCC phase boundaries.
It omits the coupled role of near-Ni3Al L12 ordering, elevated antiphase-boundary energy, planar slip, and stress concentration at jagged B2/FCC boundary tips.
No cited evidence establishes the required prior existence or aging evolution of B2/L12 chemical ordering in the proposed W-Ta-Mo-Nb-V system.
The cited coherent-nanoprecipitate evidence reports improved dislocation transmission and ductility, not ordering-induced embrittlement, so it does not support the stated mechanism.
